entities.summary:
Joseph Csaky was a Hungarian avant-garde artist, sculptor, and graphic artist, best known for his early participation in the Cubist movement as a sculptor. Csaky was one of the first sculptors in Paris to apply the principles of pictorial Cubism to his art. A pioneer of modern sculpture, Csaky is among the most important sculptors of the early 20th century.

He was an active member of the Section d'Or group between 1911 and 1914, and closely associated with Crystal Cubism, Purism, De Stijl, Abstract art, and Art Deco throughout the 1920s and 1930s. Joseph Csaky was a authors & novelists from Szeged (1888-03-18, Szeged–1971-05-01). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Csaky's pioneering work in Cubism and his association with prominent art movements had a significant impact on modern sculpture, influencing generations of artists. His contributions to the development of Crystal Cubism and Purism helped shape the course of early 20th-century art.
